stem: A child with ear pain develops tender postauricular erythema and swelling with outward displacement of the auricle. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

options.B: Uncomplicated acute otitis media without mastoid involvement

rationale: American Academy of Pediatrics clinical material describes mastoiditis with postauricular swelling and redness together with protrusion/displacement of the auricle. NCBI StatPearls similarly describes postauricular erythema, tenderness, warmth or fluctuance with protrusion of the auricle as characteristic examination findings. Therefore A is the best answer. Uncomplicated acute otitis media does not account for the postauricular inflammatory findings and displaced auricle, otitis externa primarily involves the external auditory canal, and pinna perichondritis primarily involves the auricular cartilage rather than the mastoid region.
educational_objective: Recognize postauricular inflammation with outward displacement of the auricle as a characteristic presentation of acute mastoiditis.
source_organization: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) — Red Book Online
source_locator: Case presentation: infant with tender swelling and redness over the post-auricular region, mild protrusion of the auricle, and an erythematous/bulging tympanic membrane; diagnosis case addresses mastoiditis
source_claim_supported: Postauricular swelling/redness with protrusion of the auricle in a child with ear symptoms is a characteristic clinical presentation of mastoiditis.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation, Pathophysiology, printed p.48 / PDF p.51: identify pathophysiology related to an acute or chronic condition; Illness Management: apply knowledge of client pathophysiology to illness management
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — Pathophysiology / recognition of acute mastoiditis
correction_summary: Removed the source item's unnecessary requirement for recurrent otitis media because recent or concurrent otitis media is common but is not required for acute mastoiditis. Rebuilt the stem around directly supported postauricular findings and replaced weak distractors with clinically adjacent ear disorders.
audit_findings: A is supported by current AAP clinical material and corroborated by NCBI StatPearls. B is plausible because acute otitis media commonly precedes mastoiditis, but it does not explain postauricular inflammation plus auricular displacement. C can cause ear pain but primarily affects the external auditory canal and does not match the mastoid-region pattern. D can cause an erythematous swollen tender pinna but does not account for the postauricular mastoid swelling/displacement pattern. The final item avoids implying that recurrent AOM is required, avoids treatment or imaging assumptions, and leaves one clearly best answer. Physiological Adaptation is appropriate under NCSBN 2026 Pathophysiology/Illness Management.
